subject: psychiatry
title: Eating Disorders: Anorexia Nervosa, Bulimia, and Refeeding Syndrome

steps.tx: **Anorexia nervosa** is a severe psychiatric disorder characterized by restriction of energy intake relative to requirements, leading to significantly low body weight (BMI under 18.5 kg/m2 in adults). Diagnostic criteria mandate intense fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, and severe disturbance in body image perception.
steps.say: Anorexia nervosa involves food restriction producing low body weight, paired with intense fear of weight gain and body image distortion.

vis.alt: Anorexia nervosa diagnostic criteria, neuroendocrine suppression, and systemic complications
vis.caption: Anorexia nervosa diagnostic criteria, neuroendocrine suppression, and systemic complications.

steps.tx: **Subtypes and clinical signs of anorexia** divide into the restricting type, where weight loss occurs through dieting, fasting, and excessive exercise, and the binge-eating/purging type. Physical examination reveals cachexia, hypothermia, resting sinus bradycardia, hypotension, dry scaly skin, and fine soft lanugo hair across the back and forearms.
steps.say: Anorexia divides into restricting and binge-purge subtypes. Examination demonstrates cachexia, bradycardia, hypothermia, and lanugo hair.

left.title: Restricting Subtype
points: Weight loss via rigid caloric fasting and exercise
Absence of binge eating or purging behavior
Perfectionistic, obsessive personality traits
Profound denial of severe physical emaciation

right.title: Binge-Eating / Purging Subtype
points: Regular binge eating followed by self-induced vomiting
Misuse of laxatives, diuretics, and enemas
Higher impulsivity and deliberate self-harm
Frequent electrolyte and cardiac arrhythmias

steps.tx: **Endocrine suppression in anorexia nervosa** involves functional hypothalamic amenorrhoea resulting from down-regulation of hypothalamic gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) pulses. Luteinizing hormone, follicle-stimulating hormone, and serum estradiol drop to prepubertal levels, accompanied by euthyroid sick syndrome with low triiodothyronine and elevated morning cortisol, leading to accelerated osteopenia, osteoporosis, and pathological stress fractures.
steps.say: Hypothalamic GnRH suppression drops LH, FSH, and estradiol to prepubertal levels, causing amenorrhoea, accelerated bone loss, and fractures.

vis.title: Neuroendocrine Abnormalities in Anorexia
rows: Low GnRH, LH, FSH, and estradiol
Low T3, normal/low T4, normal TSH
Elevated GH with low IGF-1 levels

steps.tx: **Bulimia nervosa** is characterized by recurrent episodes of binge eating accompanied by a subjective sense of lack of control, followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain. In marked contrast to anorexia nervosa, patients with bulimia nervosa maintain a normal or slightly elevated body mass index.
steps.say: Bulimia nervosa features recurrent binge eating with compensatory purging, while patients maintain a normal or slightly elevated body weight.

left.title: Bulimia Nervosa
points: Normal or slightly overweight body mass index
Recurrent binges with loss of eating control
Compensatory purging: vomiting or laxatives
Ego-dystonic; profound distress and shame

right.title: Anorexia Nervosa (Binge-Purge)
points: Significantly low BMI (< 18.5 kg/m2)
Binge episodes followed by purging rituals
Ego-syntonic pride in starvation control
Profound body image denial and cachexia

steps.tx: **Physical signs of recurrent purging** in bulimia nervosa include Russell sign, defined as calluses or abrasions over the dorsal knuckles from repetitive trauma against incisors during manual gagging. Patients exhibit bilateral painless parotid gland enlargement, severe dental enamel erosion on lingual tooth surfaces, and subconjunctival petechial hemorrhages.
steps.say: Purging signs include knuckle calluses from Russell sign, dental enamel erosion, and painless bilateral parotid enlargement.

vis.title: Physical Hallmarks of Self-Induced Vomiting
rows: Friction against incisor teeth during digital gag reflex induction
Lingual surfaces of maxillary incisor teeth
Chemical erosion of tooth enamel by acidic gastric secretions
Hypertrophy of acinar cells triggered by chronic acid stimulation
Tear in mucosa caused by violent emetic retching

steps.tx: **Electrolyte disturbances from purging** manifest as hypokalaemic, hypochloraemic metabolic alkalosis with paradoxical aciduria, caused by massive loss of hydrochloric acid and potassium in vomitus. Secondary hyperaldosteronism further accelerates renal potassium and hydrogen wasting, producing prolongation of the electrocardiographic QTc interval and fatal ventricular arrhythmias.
steps.say: Vomiting causes hypokalemic, hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis, triggering dangerous QTc prolongation and fatal ventricular arrhythmias.

nodes.label: Self-induced vomiting expels gastric hydrochloric acid and potassium
Hypochloraemia and extracellular metabolic alkalosis emerge
Volume depletion triggers secondary renal hyperaldosteronism
Severe hypokalaemia, U waves on ECG, and fatal ventricular fibrillation

steps.tx: **Refeeding syndrome** is a lethal medical complication occurring when malnourished anorexic patients are refed aggressively with carbohydrates, triggering massive insulin secretion. Insulin drives circulating phosphate, potassium, and magnesium into cells to phosphorylate glucose, resulting in catastrophic hypophosphataemia, acute congestive heart failure, rhabdomyolysis, and death.
steps.say: Aggressive carbohydrate feeding in severe anorexia triggers massive insulin spikes that drive phosphate into cells, causing fatal cardiac failure.

left.title: Refeeding Pathogenesis
points: Carbohydrate reintroduction triggers insulin surge
Massive intracellular uptake of phosphate and potassium
Severe acute hypophosphataemia (<1.0 mg/dL)
Total cellular ATP depletion and tissue hypoxia

right.title: Prevention Protocol
points: Start feeds low: 10 to 15 kcal/kg/day
Daily monitoring of serum phosphate, potassium, Mg
Prophylactic intravenous thiamine administration
Gradual caloric advance over seven to ten days

steps.tx: **Evidence-based psychotherapy for eating disorders** establishes family-based treatment (the Maudsley method) as the first-line therapy for adolescents with anorexia nervosa, mobilizing parents to take control of nutritional rehabilitation. For bulimia nervosa, enhanced cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT-E) paired with high-dose fluoxetine (60 mg/day) represents first-line care.
steps.say: Family-based therapy is first-line for adolescent anorexia. Bulimia nervosa responds to cognitive therapy and high-dose fluoxetine.

vis.title: Eating Disorder Management Matrix
rows: No approved drugs; olanzapine helps weight anxiety
CBT-E, MANTRA, or Specialist Supportive Care
Lisdexamfetamine or topiramate for appetite reduction
